chunks: Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled regarding a man who came with fire and set it ablaze in the house of some people, so the house burned, its inhabitants burned, and their belongings burned.
He said: 'He must compensate for the value of the house and whatever is in it, then he is to be killed.'

key_terms.بِنَارٍ: with fire; the instrument of the crime
key_terms.فَأَشْعَلَهَا: he ignited it; deliberately set it ablaze
key_terms.قِيمَةَ الدَّارِ: the value of the house; financial compensation owed
key_terms.مَتَاعُهُمْ: their belongings or property inside the house
key_terms.يُغَرَّمُ: he is made liable to pay compensation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام rule for someone who set a house on fire and killed its inhabitants?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام concerning a person who deliberately set fire to a house, resulting in the destruction of property and the deaths of its inhabitants. The ruling combines financial liability for the destroyed property with capital punishment, reflecting the gravity of deliberate arson leading to fatal harm.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5368 - In the narration of Al-Sakuni:

"Indeed, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) ruled regarding a man who came with fire and set it ablaze in the house of some people, causing the house, its inhabitants, and their belongings to burn.
Imam (as) said: 'He must compensate for the value of the house and everything in it, and then he is to be executed.'"
